key_insight: Engineered spin-chain couplings, digitally simulated on trapped-ion hardware, substantially improve quantum state-transfer fidelity over uniform nearest-neighbour interactions.
engineering_relevance: The work shows that programmable quantum processors can implement Hamiltonian-based communication protocols with lower circuit depth and faster execution by exploiting Hamiltonian commutation structure.
method: Benchmark uniform vs engineered coupling profiles with exact simulation and trapped-ion experiments.
Digitally simulate spin Hamiltonian dynamics on IonQ Forte 1 / Forte Enterprise 1 using Trotterized circuits.
Use a parallel Trotter decomposition to reduce depth and better match target evolution.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports hardware and numerical benchmarks showing that engineered interactions achieve higher state-transfer fidelity and that parallel Trotterization more faithfully reproduces the target dynamics than sequential implementations.
watch_item: Performance will still depend on hardware noise, calibration quality, and the accuracy of the digital Trotter approximation relative to the ideal Hamiltonian evolution.
paper_title: Spin Chain Quantum Communication on a Trapped-Ion Processor
